hero.title: Zero-Tick Engine: a pulse only when something happens
hero.desc: Two traces like a heart monitor. Top, a classic build: an identical spike every 100 ms, whether anything happens or not. Bottom, Zero-Tick: a flat line with a single spike exactly when something happens: a hit, a buff ending, a player entering.
hero.classic_sub: works every 100 ms, even when nothing happens

tick.title: Fixed 100 ms tick versus Zero-Tick
tick.desc: Top: a loop that ticks every 100 ms. Events that arrive between ticks wait for the next tick, up to 100 ms, and ticks with nothing to do still run: 12 idle ticks out of 16. Bottom: Zero-Tick handles each event the moment it arrives and does nothing in between: no idle work, no added delay.

race.title: Sleep and a hit at the same moment: classic build versus Zero-Tick
race.desc: A mage casts Sleep on a monster while a warrior hits it. If Sleep lands first, the hit wakes the monster and Sleep is wasted; if the hit lands first, the monster falls asleep. Left, a classic build: Sleep runs on one pool thread and the hit on another, both reach the monster at once, and the result changes from run to run. Right, Zero-Tick: the partition thread takes both from one queue in arrival order, hit first, then Sleep, so the monster falls asleep every time.

dupe.title: Item dupe: classic build versus Zero-Tick
dupe.desc: A player owns one rare sword and, at the same moment, sells it to an NPC shop and gives it away in a trade. Top, a classic build: the sale and the trade run on two threads, both check the inventory at once and both see the sword, so both complete: the player gets adena and the second player gets the sword, and the sword now exists twice. Bottom, Zero-Tick: one partition thread takes the two operations in arrival order; the sale takes the sword, the trade finds no item and is rejected, and exactly one sword remains.
dupe.left_caption: one missed lock in the code = a dupe

spaces.title: Every space on its own thread
spaces.desc: The open world, two instances and an olympiad, each a separate space with its own thread, all asleep. A mass battle keeps the open world busy; meanwhile an olympiad match wakes the olympiad, which runs smoothly on its own thread. Later a boss wakes one instance. The other instance sleeps the whole time.
spaces.caption: Every space runs on its own thread and wakes only when something happens
spaces.note: Massive world battles never slow down the Olympiad
